solution_overview:
A concert venue tracks no-shows for two ticket types: General Admission (GA) and VIP. A ticket is selected at random from the total sold. We are given the counts for each category.

Let $N_{\text{GA}}$ be the number of General Admission tickets sold and $N_{\text{VIP}}$ be the number of VIP tickets sold. Let $N_{\text{GA,NS}}$ be the number of GA no-shows and $N_{\text{VIP,NS}}$ be the number of VIP no-shows.

The given data are:
$N_{\text{GA}} = 8000$
$N_{\text{VIP}} = 2000$
$N_{\text{GA,NS}} = 1200$
$N_{\text{VIP,NS}} = 100$

Total tickets sold are $N_{\text{Total}} = N_{\text{GA}} + N_{\text{VIP}}$.
$$N_{\text{Total}} = 8000 + 2000 = 10000$$

Total no-shows are $N_{\text{NS,Total}} = N_{\text{GA,NS}} + N_{\text{VIP,NS}}$.
$$N_{\text{NS,Total}} = 1200 + 100 = 1300$$

Total attendees (not no-shows) are $N_{\text{Attended,Total}} = N_{\text{Total}} - N_{\text{NS,Total}}$.
$$N_{\text{Attended,Total}} = 10000 - 1300 = 8700$$

Probabilities are calculated by dividing the number of favorable outcomes by the total number of possible outcomes.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

The probability that a randomly selected ticket holder is a no-show is the total number of no-shows divided by the total number of tickets sold.
$$P(\text{no-show}) = \frac{N_{\text{NS,Total}}}{N_{\text{Total}}}$$ 
$$P(\text{no-show}) = \frac{1300}{10000}$$ 
$$P(\text{no-show}) = 0.13 = 13\%$$ 

The claim is that this probability is greater than $14\%$. Since $13\% \not> 14\%$, the statement is False.

**B.** → False

The probability of a no-show given the ticket is VIP is found by dividing the number of VIP no-shows by the total number of VIP tickets.
$$P(\text{no-show} \mid \text{VIP}) = \frac{N_{\text{VIP,NS}}}{N_{\text{VIP}}}$$ 
$$P(\text{no-show} \mid \text{VIP}) = \frac{100}{2000}$$ 
$$P(\text{no-show} \mid \text{VIP}) = 0.05 = 5\%$$ 

The probability of a no-show given the ticket is General Admission is found by dividing the number of GA no-shows by the total number of GA tickets.
$$P(\text{no-show} \mid \text{GA}) = \frac{N_{\text{GA,NS}}}{N_{\text{GA}}}$$ 
$$P(\text{no-show} \mid \text{GA}) = \frac{1200}{8000}$$ 
$$P(\text{no-show} \mid \text{GA}) = 0.15 = 15\%$$ 

The claim is that $P(\text{no-show} \mid \text{VIP}) > P(\text{no-show} \mid \text{GA})$. Since $5\% \not> 15\%$, the statement is False.

**C.** → False

This is a conditional probability asking for the likelihood that the ticket is VIP, given that a no-show occurred. We use the total number of VIP no-shows relative to the total number of no-shows.
$$P(\text{VIP} \mid \text{no-show}) = \frac{N_{\text{VIP,NS}}}{N_{\text{NS,Total}}}$$ 
$$P(\text{VIP} \mid \text{no-show}) = \frac{100}{1300}$$ 
$$P(\text{VIP} \mid \text{no-show}) \approx 0.07692 \approx 7.69\%$$ 

The claim is that this probability is greater than $10\%$. Since $7.69\% \not> 10\%$, the statement is False.

**D.** → False

The probability that the ticket is General Admission given a no-show occurred is the number of GA no-shows divided by the total number of no-shows.
$$P(\text{GA} \mid \text{no-show}) = \frac{N_{\text{GA,NS}}}{N_{\text{NS,Total}}}$$ 
$$P(\text{GA} \mid \text{no-show}) = \frac{1200}{1300}$$ 
$$P(\text{GA} \mid \text{no-show}) \approx 0.9231 \approx 92.31\%$$ 

From the previous calculation for Statement C, $P(\text{VIP} \mid \text{no-show}) \approx 7.69\%$. The claim is $P(\text{GA} \mid \text{no-show}) < P(\text{VIP} \mid \text{no-show})$. Since $92.31\% \not< 7.69\%$, the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The probability that a ticket holder attends means they are not a no-show. This is the complement of being a no-show. We can compute it as $1 - P(\text{no-show})$.
$$P(\text{attends}) = 1 - P(\text{no-show})$$
From Statement A, $P(\text{no-show}) = 0.13$.
$$P(\text{attends}) = 1 - 0.13$$ 
$$P(\text{attends}) = 0.87 = 87\%$$ 

The claim is that this probability is greater than $88\%$. Since $87\% \not> 88\%$, the statement is False.
